basis: frozen (AI-reviewed baseline), reviewed by ChatGPT (GPT-6, AI reviewer), as stated in its review relayed by the repository owner on 2026-11-20

requirements.quote: planning is the default; only a request to build or implement authorizes implementation, and only within that scope.
requirements.reason: Same rule stated in authorization reading.

requirements.quote: Follow existing task authorization without repeated approval.
requirements.reason: Present, but the logic asks the user to authorize whenever authorization is unclear, which can ask even when existing authorization exists.

requirements.quote: deploy, publish, install tools, or delegate beyond their own applicable permissions
requirements.reason: Contract prohibition plus a logic branch that asks for approval and holds dependent work.

requirements.quote: identify the subject repository, outcome, selected work IDs, constraints, and exclusions.
exec #inspect inspect applicable instructions, code, contracts, tests, and prototypes from checks as inspection
requirements.reason: Inspection is required and ordered before design writing.

requirements.quote: preserve authoritative documents, IDs, and project vocabulary
keep current state, target state, and migration distinct
requirements.reason: Contract always rule, plus a never rule on treating documentation or mock data as working behavior.

requirements.quote: label each discovery and proposed mechanism as exactly one of required now, existing dependency, unresolved prerequisite, or deferred enhancement.
expand or replace scope because of a discovery alone
resolve from available evidence, state consequential assumptions, and use reversible ordinary choices to continue.

apply commitment record with increments as commitment
    write commitment with registry
requirements.reason: The record is required, but no ordering constraint puts it before the commitment itself. It is only written to the registry.

requirements.quote: if a missing answer changes the outcome or authority and available evidence cannot resolve it:
requirements.reason: Clarification is limited to that condition.

requirements.quote: preserve settled user decisions
only when its condition holds.
requirements.reason: Reference reads are conditional, from the References section.

requirements.quote: follow trigger, state transitions, and result, including relevant failure, retry, cancellation, and recovery
one authority per state set or an explicit coordination protocol
research uncertainty that could change the design; preserve valid existing choices
label doubles with their simulated guarantees, limits, and replacement conditions
requirements.reason: Contract always rule, plus a never rule on treating doubles as operational integration.

requirements.quote: keep requirements, invariants, assumptions, source inspection, executed tests, measurements, and proof distinct, and mark unexecuted checks
for the one authoritative work registry in the subject project.
requirements.reason: Registry entries step, with write to the registry.

requirements.quote: assemble scope, linked design, ownership and contracts, research-backed choices, ordered increments, and blockers
requirements.reason: Design assembly step. The planned return carries the readiness label for ready versus conditional.

requirements.quote: design readiness and a first working increment do not mean the milestone is complete.
requirements.reason: Contract never rule, plus verify that every selected acceptance criterion passed.

requirements.quote: explain excluding any material concern without adding unrelated scope.
match consumer assumptions to provider guarantees or explicit unresolved conditions
resolve consequential reuse before detailing custom internals
requirements.reason: Resolve choices step. Its position in the sequence puts it before the later design steps.

requirements.quote: stop at adopted providers' public boundaries and allocate required fit gaps.
screens, nouns, directories, and workflow steps do not dictate components
components do not dictate files, packages, services, processes, or teams.
split only where different decisions need hiding, authority changes hands, protection or lifecycle differs, or coupling prevents a coherent increment
resolve shared interface work before claiming independence.

if new evidence changed the scope, behavior, or contracts:
    return to iterate
requirements.reason: The iterate loop covers it. No explicit statement not to freeze requirements, but the loop implements it.

requirements.quote: mark the increment ready; outcome, contracts, prerequisites, and checks are usable and consequential decisions resolved
separate prototype appearance and interaction requirements from simulated behavior.

introduced.behavior: Asks the user to authorize implementation when authorization is unclear, which is a new question to the user.
introduced.quote: ask user to authorize implementation within this scope

introduced.behavior: Asks the user to approve deployment, publication, tool installation, or delegation. The source only said they follow their own permissions.
introduced.quote: ask user to approve deployment, publication, tool installation, or delegation

introduced.behavior: Writes design documents to the project. The source did not explicitly require this for design-only work.
Writes the commitment record to the registry.
Ends with a blocked return when a failure persists. The source has no such return.
Fixes a design-before-implementation order and requires acceptance checks to run before the built return.
